clarity.instructions: How easily can an AI coding agent understand `section_text` on first read and know exactly what is true or what it must do?
criteria: The meaning cannot be recovered: it depends on unstated context, undefined abbreviations, run-together words without spaces, or references the reader cannot resolve
The main point can be worked out only after rereading, decoding compressed wording, or guessing what vague references mean
Plain sentences; every rule, fact or step can be acted on or checked directly on first read

filler.instructions: How much of `section_text` is abstract, emphatic, slogan-like or repeated wording that gives an agent nothing concrete to check or do?
criteria: Almost all content is concrete: specific rules, commands, file paths, names, numbers or observable results
Concrete content with some abstract principles, emphatic adjectives or restated rules that add no checkable meaning
Mostly abstract principles, buzzwords, slogans or repetition, with few concrete checkable rules

status.instructions: Considering `project_context`, what role does `section_text` play for someone doing the project's next piece of work?

criteria.current_rule: States a rule, requirement or design decision that still governs how the current Go + FLTK + in-process libmpv Windows product or the agent workflow must work
criteria.current_progress: Records the current state of in-progress work, open gates or next steps
criteria.historical_record: Records past events, completed loops, old evidence, measurements or decisions that no longer drive current work
criteria.superseded_design: Describes a design, tool or process that project_context says was removed or replaced (Wails, Svelte, Fyne, external MPV process and JSON IPC, NSIS, WebView) as if it were still the plan
criteria.mixed: Interleaves current rules or progress with historical or superseded material so the reader must separate them

tool_specific.instructions: Does `section_text` require or assume one specific AI coding tool, vendor or model (for example Codex, OpenAI, GPT, Claude, OpenCode, a named model version or its configuration files) instead of stating a tool-neutral rule?

criteria.true: Names or depends on a particular AI coding tool, vendor, model or its configuration
criteria.false: Tool-neutral, or mentions no AI coding tool at all

needed.instructions: How often would an AI agent implementing the next product feature in this project need to read `section_text`?
criteria: Never: it only serves audit history or traceability
Only in a specific situation, such as a release, a security change, a CI failure or a platform port
Routinely: it defines how ordinary feature work must be done or what the product must do
